sentences.text: This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondent under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27.05.2023 at about 10.00am.

2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 27.05.2023 at about 10.00am the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-JZ-3749 from his house to office in a moderate speed by observing all the traffic rules and regulations passing on either side of the said road, when he reached near Chikkasanne Gate stopped his motorcycle on the extreme right side of the road to go towards service road, at that juncture a KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-0965 came from Devanahalli side towards Bengaluru side with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to New Manasa Hospital, Devanahalli Town, Bengaluru Rural District, wherein treated conservatively and thereafter discharged with advice to take complete bed rest and to continue follow up treatment.

So far he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards hospital charges, medicines, attendant charges, conveyance,
nourishing food and other incidental expenses.
Due to accidental injuries, he cannot stand or walk for longer duration and getting severe pain all over the body.

4. It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy was working in a Private Firm and earning Rs.40,000/- per month and was contributing his entire income for welfare and maintenance of his family.
Due to accidental injuries, he is unable to concentration on his avocation as before the accident.

The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent drivcing by the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-0965 and Devanahalli Traffic Police Station, North East Traffic Sub-Division, Bengaluru have registered a case against the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-0965 in their Cr.No.110/2023 p/u/Secs.279, 337 of IPC.

entities.text: Devanahalli Traffic Police Station, North East Traffic Sub-Division,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The respondent being the RC owner of the KSRTC Bus is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant compensation as prayed in the petition.
5. In response tot he notice, the respondent appeared before this Court and filed written statement.
5A. The respondent has filed the written statement denying the entire petition averments.

As per the statement of the Driver of the KSRTC Bus is concerned, the respondent submits that on 27.5.2023,
the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F- Sharath Kumar H M vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142204520/
2 0965 was proceeding from Devanahalli towards Bengaluru, driven by its driver slowly, carefully on the left side of the road observing all the traffic rules and regulations. When the said KSRTC bus proceeding slowly reached near Chikkasonnenahalli Gate 'U' Turn junction one motorcycle bearing Reg.NO.KA-40-JZ-3749 ridden by its rider without following traffic rules and regulations without wearing helmet with rash and negligent manner came from Yelahanka side while took turn at the 'U'
turn one Car was also standing in 'U' turn waiting for clearance of main road vehicles, at the same time the rider of the said motorcycle over take the said Car without observing the main road vehicle,
immediately while crossing the 'U' turn junction and dashed against front right side of the slowly moving KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-0965.
Due to impact the rider of the motorcycle fell down and sustained injuries.
The accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent manner of the rider of the said motorcycle as stated above.
Hence, the driver of the KSRTC Bus was not at all responsible for the accident and the Respondent is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further denied, the age, occupation, medical expenses etc., Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant.
Accordingly, the respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 27.05.2023 at 10.00am due to rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 40-F-0965 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
 Issue No.2: Whether the  petitioner is entitled for  Compensation?
If so, what is the  quantum?
From whom?
Issue No.3: What Order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Nine documents as Exs.P1 to P9.
The Driver of the KSRTC Bus got examined himself as RW.1 and did not mark any documents on their behalf.
8. The Court has heard the arguments canvassed by both sides counsel.
9. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above points are as follows:
Issue No.1 :Partly in affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the foregoing #REASONS#
10.
Issue No.1:-
In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Nine documents as Exs.P1 to P9.

The Driver of the KSRTC Bus got Sharath Kumar H M vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142204520/
3 examined himself as RW.1 but, did not mark any documents on his behalf.

sentences.text: The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
11. The chief examination of the PW.1 is nothing but a repetition of plaint averments.
The PW.1 has been subjected to cross examination.

During the cross examination of PW.1, he has admitted that,
the bike belongs to him only and it was insured.
He gave complaint on the same day of the accident.
He further denied other material suggestions of the counsel in the cross examination.
12. It is the specific defense of the driver that the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself.
In this regard he has examined himself as RW.1.
RW.1 has been subjected to cross examination.
During the cross examination of RW.1, he has admitted that the charge sheet filed against him.
He has not lodged any complaint about the accident.
He further denied other material suggestions of the counsel in the cross examination 13.
The petitioner has totally relied on the police documents to establish the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle's driver.
It is no doubt the police have submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus Driver after thorough investigation.
The spot sketch appended to the spot mahazar indicates that the accident was occurred at inter-junction of Bengaluru-Devanahalli Road.
The mahazar indicates that the petitioner ought to have reached the service by crossing the main road.
The accident spot is at the edge of median.
It is undisputed fact that the offending vehicle was proceeding from Devanahalli to Bengaluru Side.
The accident spot clearly depicts that the petitioner has proceeding towards his service road without observing oncoming vehicles.
In the same time, the driver of the bus has also taken minimal care where ever the inter-junction have existed in the road.
The petitioner has not made any attempt to produce the motor vehicle inspection report through out the proceedings.
So, it is appears to the Court that, the accident was not occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the offending vehicle.

Hence the Tribunal fixes the negligence at 75% of the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle and 25%
on the motorcyclist or petitioner.
So, I hold issue No.1 partly in affirmative.
14. Issue No.2: the claimant has produced Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.5.

It shows that the claimant has sustained (i) Abrasion over right foot,
(ii) Pain in hip which are simple in nature.

So, I am of the opinion that though the claimant is able to prove that he has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident but he has failed to prove that he had sustained permanent disability due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Considering the contents of wound certificate and nature of injury sustained in the accident, it can be presumed that claimant has taken treatment for above said injury and he got recovered.
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.7 for a sum of Rs.17,994/-.
Out of these bills, Bill No.13 and Bill No.2 are the same.
So they will be consider only one bill.
As such, after deduction of Rs.4,000/- in total amount then it comes to Rs.13,994/-.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
The petitioner did not produce discharge summary to show the duration of the treatment.

Therefore, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident, nature of treatment taken by him and also amount spent towards treatment, I am of the firm opinion that awarding a sum of Rs.50,000/- as global compensation under only one Sharath Kumar H M vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142204520/
4 conventional head meets the ends of justice.

sentences.text: In the said amount, 25% should be deducted as tribunal fixed the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
In view of, I answer issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
15. Issue No.3:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part.

The respondent is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.37,500/-
(Rupees Thirty Seven Thousand Five Hundred only) together interest @ 6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the said amount within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
On deposit of compensation, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw entire amount with interest as awarded amount is meager one.
The office is directed to release the entire amount to petitioner or PW.1 with interest through e-payment with proper identification.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.

The advocate fee of Rs.1,000/-
 fixed.
Draw the award accordingly.
